meta.title: Technology Deep Dive — Bhoomi Bytes
meta.description: Explore the full technical architecture of Bhoomi Bytes: ESP32 microcontrollers, soil and climate sensors, real-time data pipelines, AI recommendation engine, and weather API integration.

hero.title: How Bhoomi Bytes Works Under the Hood
hero.subtitle: From a sensor buried in the soil to an AI-generated irrigation recommendation on a farmer's phone — every layer of the stack, explained.

overview.title: Five Layers. One Integrated Platform.
overview.subtitle: Bhoomi Bytes is built as a layered IoT + AI stack. Each layer has a single responsibility and communicates with the next through well-defined interfaces.

layers.name: Sensing Layer
layers.desc: Physical sensors deployed in the field collect soil and climate data continuously.

layers.name: Edge Processing
layers.desc: ESP32 microcontrollers aggregate, filter, and transmit sensor readings over Wi-Fi.

layers.name: Data Pipeline
layers.desc: A backend API ingests, validates, stores, and streams real-time telemetry data.

layers.name: Intelligence Layer
layers.desc: AI models and weather API data are combined to generate crop-specific recommendations.

layers.name: Actuation & UI
layers.desc: Recommendations drive pump control commands and are surfaced on the farmer dashboard.

hardware.title: ESP32 + Sensor Array
hardware.intro: The field unit is built around the ESP32 — a low-cost, Wi-Fi-enabled microcontroller with dual-core processing and deep-sleep modes for power efficiency. Each unit supports up to 8 sensors on a single deployment.

specs.label: Processor
specs.value: Xtensa dual-core LX6, up to 240 MHz

sensors.name: Soil Moisture Sensor
sensors.desc: Capacitive design avoids corrosion issues common with resistive sensors. Measures volumetric water content using dielectric permittivity of soil.

sensors.name: Temperature & Humidity
sensors.desc: Measures ambient air temperature and relative humidity. Used for evapotranspiration calculations and disease risk modeling.

sensors.name: Soil pH Sensor
sensors.desc: Electrochemical sensor measuring hydrogen ion activity. Critical for nutrient availability modeling — most crops require pH 6.0–7.5.

sensors.name: TDS / EC Sensor
sensors.desc: Measures total dissolved solids as a proxy for soil nutrient concentration and salinity. Alerts when fertilizer runoff or saline intrusion is detected.

sensors.name: Light Intensity
sensors.desc: Measures photosynthetically active radiation (PAR) proxy. Used to adjust irrigation scheduling — high light increases evapotranspiration demand.

firmware.title: ESP32 Firmware Architecture
firmware.intro: The firmware is written in C++ using the Arduino framework on top of ESP-IDF. It runs a cooperative task loop with three primary responsibilities: sensor polling, local buffering, and MQTT transmission.

tasks.name: Sensor Poll Task
tasks.desc: Reads all connected sensors via ADC and I²C. Applies moving-average filtering to reduce noise. Stores readings in a circular buffer.

tasks.name: Transmission Task
tasks.desc: Aggregates buffered readings into a JSON payload. Publishes to the MQTT broker over TLS. Retries with exponential backoff on failure.

tasks.name: Command Listener
tasks.desc: Listens on the device command topic for pump control instructions. Executes relay toggle immediately on receipt. Acknowledges back to broker.

tasks.name: OTA Update Task
tasks.desc: Checks for firmware updates on boot and on a daily schedule. Downloads and applies updates over HTTPS without interrupting sensor operation.

pipeline.title: From Field to Database in Under 2 Seconds
pipeline.intro: The backend pipeline is designed for low-latency ingestion, real-time streaming to the dashboard, and reliable long-term storage for AI model training.

stages.name: MQTT Ingestion
stages.desc: ESP32 devices publish JSON payloads to topic `bhoomi/{device_id}/telemetry`. The broker authenticates devices via client certificates and forwards to the processing service.

stages.name: Validation & Parsing
stages.desc: Incoming payloads are validated against a JSON schema. Out-of-range values are flagged as anomalies. Timestamps are normalized to UTC. Malformed payloads are rejected and logged.

stages.name: Time-Series Storage
stages.desc: Validated readings are written to InfluxDB for high-frequency time-series queries (dashboard charts, trend analysis). Aggregated daily summaries are written to PostgreSQL for AI training data.

stages.name: Real-Time Streaming
stages.desc: A WebSocket server pushes new readings to connected dashboard clients within 500ms of ingestion. The live demo uses Server-Sent Events for the sensor gauge updates.

stages.name: AI Trigger
stages.desc: Each new telemetry batch triggers the AI recommendation engine asynchronously. Results are stored and pushed to the dashboard alongside the raw sensor data.

ai.title: AI Recommendation Engine
ai.intro: The recommendation engine combines real-time sensor data, historical field data, crop-specific agronomic knowledge, and live weather forecasts to generate actionable, context-aware recommendations.

models.name: Irrigation Decision Model
models.desc: Combines agronomic threshold rules (crop-specific field capacity and wilting point values) with a gradient-boosted classifier trained on historical irrigation outcomes. Outputs: irrigate now / schedule / hold.

models.name: Crop Stress Detector
models.desc: Monitors sensor readings for patterns associated with water stress, nutrient deficiency, or disease onset. Uses an isolation forest model trained on labeled stress events from agricultural research datasets.

models.name: Irrigation Volume Calculator
models.desc: Calculates the precise water volume needed to bring soil moisture to field capacity, accounting for soil texture, root depth, and ET₀. Based on the FAO-56 crop water requirement methodology.

weather.title: OpenWeatherMap API Integration
weather.intro: Live weather data is fetched every 30 minutes per farm location and used to adjust irrigation recommendations in real time. Rain forecasts prevent unnecessary irrigation; heat forecasts trigger pre-emptive watering.

endpoints.name: Current Weather
endpoints.use: Real-time temperature, humidity, wind speed for ET₀ calculation

endpoints.name: 5-Day Forecast
endpoints.use: 3-hour interval forecasts for irrigation scheduling over the next 5 days

endpoints.name: UV Index
endpoints.use: Solar radiation proxy for evapotranspiration and crop stress modeling

logic.action: Delay sprinkler scheduling, recommend drip instead
Increase ET₀ estimate, shorten irrigation interval

actuation.title: Smart Pump Control
actuation.intro: The ESP32 controls a relay module connected to the irrigation pump motor. Commands flow from the dashboard or AI engine through the MQTT broker to the device in under 1 second.

features.title: Instant Remote Control
features.desc: Toggle the pump on/off from the dashboard or mobile app. Command latency under 1 second over a stable Wi-Fi connection.

features.title: Auto-Off Scheduling
features.desc: Set irrigation duration (5, 10, 15, or 30 minutes). The ESP32 enforces the timer locally — pump stops even if connectivity is lost.

features.title: AI-Triggered Automation
features.desc: When the AI engine determines irrigation is needed, it can automatically trigger the pump (with farmer opt-in) or send a push notification for manual approval.

features.title: Safety Interlocks
features.desc: Pump is blocked if soil moisture is already above field capacity, if a rain event is in progress, or if the device has been offline for more than 10 minutes.

items.title: LoRaWAN Support
items.desc: Add LoRa radio modules for farms without reliable Wi-Fi. Range: 2–15 km in rural terrain.

items.title: Edge AI Inference
items.desc: Run lightweight TFLite models directly on the ESP32-S3 for offline recommendations when connectivity is unavailable.

items.title: Satellite Imagery Integration
items.desc: Ingest NDVI data from Sentinel-2 to detect crop health patterns at field scale, not just sensor point measurements.

items.title: Multi-Node Mesh Network
items.desc: ESP-MESH protocol to create self-healing sensor networks across large farms without additional infrastructure.
